title: Hyphae v2: Hash-Chained Verbatim Quotation — A Verifiable Provenance Layer for Grounded Retrieval
description: Hyphae is a cognitive substrate that answers retrieval queries by emitting byte-identical quotations of stored memory fragments over a SHA-256 hash-chained journal, with no large language model in the cognition path. Its distinguishing property is verifiable provenance: every output span can be independently audited back to named, unaltered source fragments, with an external Ed25519 head anchor closing the chain-aware adversary. The accompanying preprint studies verifiable provenance as an addable layer for any extractive retrieval system. A trivial echo control (and echo+journal) shows that measured correctness and grounding are properties of verbatim quotation rather than of the system; evaluation spans 18 LLM-based configurations (six models x three retrieval modes) across two corpora, plus a minimal tamper-detection benchmark (four tampering modes x two adversaries). This Zenodo record archives the full repository: the Rust substrate, the LLM+RAG comparator, all result envelopes, the provenance experiment, and the LaTeX source and PDF of the preprint.
